facts.description: Read by the platform when the request arrives. Only a question about the person's own data uses it. Without it, such a question gets the fixed fallback.

previous.description: The turn before this one. Context for the question lane only: the Planner never builds request text from it.

token.description: Sent back as the X-Callback-Token header, never in the URL. The handler must compare it in constant time, bind it to this run_id and task_id, and give it an expiry.
token.title: Token

url.description: Where the agent posts each event. It names only the run and the task.
url.title: Url

alternative.description: The nearest thing the Planner can set up, with every part checked. None when nothing comes close, so the only next step is Ask the team.

cant.description: Each part the platform can't do.
cant.title: Cant

needs.description: new_tool when the part is in a system the platform already reaches, such as Jira or GitHub, so a tool would have to be built and the team decides. new_system when it names a system or source the platform doesn't reach, or names none.

note.description: Why it can't do it yet.
note.title: Note

system.description: The system the part names, in plain words, such as Jira or email. None when it names none.
system.title: System

text.description: The part the platform can't do, in plain words.
text.title: Text

cant.description: The verb phrase a refusal uses after I can't, or None when it is ready.
cant.title: Cant

focus.description: True for what software versioning uses: checking releases, asking for a yes, creating the upgrade ticket. Home's lists show only these.
focus.title: Focus

needs_model.description: True when the agents do it with the AI model, so it needs one connected.
needs_model.title: Needs Model

plain.description: The capability in an Operator's words.
plain.title: Plain

platform.description: True for what the platform does by itself, which Home leaves out of its lists.
platform.title: Platform

state.description: The base state. A missing key or a system that is not answering is worked out from the connection, not here.

system.description: The system it reaches, in an Operator's words.
system.title: System

tools.description: The tools that do it. Empty unless it is ready.
tools.title: Tools

why.description: Why it can't be done, in plain words, or None when it is ready.
why.title: Why

tool.description: The one tool this block uses, or None for a block that only thinks.

CardDraft.description:
What the model drafted, unchecked. Tool ids and input kinds are plain text here, because
the platform checks the draft and shows an Operator every problem before it can be saved.
CardDraft.title: CardDraft

kind.description: What the value is. A write tool's target comes from the card's one input of the kind that tool needs, such as jira_project for jira.create_ticket.

values.description: One value for each of the card's inputs, by name.
values.title: Values

agents.description: The agents the Planner brings in, in the order they work.
agents.title: Agents

CarryForward.description: What a run hands to the next run of its use case.

last_run_on.description: The day the workflow's last finished run started, in the task's time_zone, so it is the day the run list shows. None when it has no finished run yet. The platform sets it on a task. It is empty in a task's output.
last_run_on.title: Last Run On

CarryForward.title: CarryForward

workflow_words.description: The words of the task that name one workflow, as it wrote them. The platform matches them to a workflow. None when the question is about all of them.
workflow_words.title: Workflow Words

values.description: Only values the task itself says, by input name. Never invented.
values.title: Values

base_url.description: The address to send with this style in a ModelAccess.
base_url.title: Base Url

needs.description: The ids of the capabilities the example uses.
needs.title: Needs

name.description: The software as a person wrote it, such as Kubernetes.
name.title: Name

detail.description: One plain sentence for people about this software.
detail.title: Detail

full_name.description: The owner/name GitHub answered for the saved repository at this check. It differs from the saved one when GitHub renamed or moved the repository and redirects the old name. None when GitHub was not asked or did not answer.

new_versions.description: Releases newer than our version, newest first. Empty unless the state is behind or already_raised.
new_versions.title: New Versions

newest.description: The newest release at the source that matches the tag pattern. None when the source could not be read or has no such release.
newest.title: Newest

not_found.description: True when GitHub answered that the saved repository does not exist (404). Nothing says where it went.
not_found.title: Not Found

suggested.description: True when the name suggests a fast model, which suits summaries.
suggested.title: Suggested

matches.description: Every project the name could mean. More than one means the person chooses. A match is a guess from a reviewed list, never a certainty.
matches.title: Matches

message.description: Plain words for an Operator. Never the token or GitHub's own error text.
message.title: Message

expires_at.description: When GitHub says the token stops working. Null for a token with no end date and when no token is set.
expires_at.title: Expires At

using_token.description: False when no token is set and GitHub is read anonymously, 60 calls an hour.
using_token.title: Using Token

ref.description: The repository whose releases are read, as owner/name.

api_key.description: Used for this call only. The runtime never stores or logs it.
api_key.title: Api Key

base_url.description: The address the chat client calls, as Connect found it.
base_url.title: Base Url

style.description: How to call the model: Anthropic's Messages API or OpenAI's Chat Completions API.

message.description: Plain words for an Operator. Never the provider's own error text, which can quote the address or the key.
message.title: Message

total.description: The count Home shows under Needs you.
total.title: Total

cant.description: Each part it can't do. Every one needs a new tool.
cant.title: Cant

rows.description: The part the platform can do, as a card: the request with each part it can't do swapped for the nearest thing it can, or left for the person to choose.
rows.title: Rows

note.description: Why it can't do it, in plain words.
note.title: Note

PlannerFacts.description:
What the platform holds for the signed-in person at the moment of the question. A section
that is None was not sent, and the answer may not claim to have looked at it.
PlannerFacts.title: PlannerFacts

PreviousTurn.description: The turn before the one being answered, sent by the Portal with the next typed request.

answer.description: The text of the Planner's answer, when it had one.
answer.title: Answer

request.description: What the person typed, or the chip's words.
request.title: Request

software.description: The software the Planner named in its answer.
software.title: Software

PreviousTurn.title: PreviousTurn

subject.description: The id of the input this write is about, such as a watched software's id. The platform uses it to follow the write once it is done.
subject.title: Subject

looked_at.description: The sections of the facts the answer used, kept only when they were sent.
looked_at.title: Looked At

text.description: The model's own words, from the facts sent and nothing else (ADR 0042).
text.title: Text

rest.description: The request without the words that asked to skip a yes, so it can be set up with one. Empty when nothing is left.
rest.title: Rest

said.description: The words that asked to skip a yes, as the request wrote them, so the refusal names the part. Empty only when the model said so without quoting them.
said.title: Said

name.description: The Planner's guess at a name. The Portal shows it as filled in by the Planner, with Rename.
name.title: Name

rows.description: One schedule row, then at least one row for what to look for, what to do and where, in that order. None is cant_do. A time the task doesn't say is missing, never guessed.
rows.title: Rows

newest.description: The newest stable release tag that the tag rule counts. None when there is none.
newest.title: Newest

releases.description: Whether the project has a stable release that the request's tag rule counts. With none, a watch would have nothing to compare.
releases.title: Releases

repo.description: A GitHub project that exists, as owner/name, at the address GitHub gives it now. Checked just now.

what.description: What the project is, in plain words, so the person can tell matches apart.
what.title: What

why.description: Where the guess came from, in plain words, for the person to read.
why.title: Why

message.description: What went wrong with GitHub, in plain words. No project is offered, because nothing unchecked is shown.
message.title: Message

message.description: The list has no such name, or GitHub found none of its projects.
message.title: Message

awaiting_approval.description: True while an earlier check's ticket for this software waits for an Approver. No new ticket is proposed meanwhile.
awaiting_approval.title: Awaiting Approval

from_first_check.description: True when our_version is only the newest release an earlier first check read, not a version anyone gave. A ticket then says so instead of calling it the version the team runs.
from_first_check.title: From First Check

open_ticket.description: The ticket already raised for this software and not yet done, such as MOCK-7. While there is one, no new ticket is proposed.
open_ticket.title: Open Ticket

our_version.description: The version the team runs now. None means the newest release becomes the starting point.
our_version.title: Our Version

TagPattern.description: Which release tags count. Only a pattern from a fixed list is accepted, never one the caller writes. Allowed values: `^(?:[vV]|docker-v|n8n@|langchain==)?\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`, `^[vV]?\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`, `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`.

findings.description: When a watchlist check could read none of its software: one finding for each, with its own reason. Empty for any other failure.
findings.title: Findings

findings.description: One per watched software, in the order of the inputs. Empty for a card run.
findings.title: Findings

model.description: The model that writes the summary. Without one, the runtime uses its own settings, then its template. A reused task_id is matched without this field, so a key replaced between two tries of one task does not make it a different task.

time_zone.description: The zone the team works in, such as Asia/Singapore. The agents' today and every plain day they read or send, last_run_on included, are days in it.
time_zone.title: Time Zone

input_schema.description: The arguments the model sends. A write tool never takes its target.
input_schema.title: Input Schema

note.description: Why the part is changed, missing or can't be done. Usually None when it is understood.
note.title: Note

text.description: What the Planner read, in plain words. Empty when the part is missing, and can be empty when it can't be done.
text.title: Text

awaiting_approval.description: True when a ticket for it waits for an Approver's yes.
awaiting_approval.title: Awaiting Approval

checked_at.description: When the software was last checked. None when never.
checked_at.title: Checked At

newest_version.description: The newest release read from the source. None when unread.
newest_version.title: Newest Version

open_ticket.description: The upgrade ticket that is open, if any.
open_ticket.title: Open Ticket

our_version.description: The version the team runs. None means Not known.
our_version.title: Our Version

our_version_source.description: How the version the team runs was set. None when not known.
our_version_source.title: Our Version Source

our_version_ticket.description: The ticket that moved the version, if any.
our_version_ticket.title: Our Version Ticket

problem.description: Why the last check could not read it.
problem.title: Problem

state.description: The state in the words the Software page shows.
state.title: State

also.description: The rest of a request that also asks for a workflow, such as a weekly ticket list, offered next. None when the request is only about the software.
also.title: Also

software.description: The software the task names, as it wrote it.
software.title: Software

word.description: The word that made the Planner think so, as the task wrote it.
word.title: Word

last_run.description: The state of the newest run, in the words the Portal uses.
last_run.title: Last Run
